How NovelNest writes and reviews original content

Editorial Policy

How NovelNest creates original guides and recommendations, handles corrections, and keeps editorial content separate from advertising.

Original work

NovelNest Reading Desk articles are created for NovelNest readers. They are written to explain reading habits, genre conventions, discovery methods, and practical ways to choose or organize web novels. Editorial pages are not copied from novel chapters or publisher descriptions.

Editorial independence

Recommendations and guides are chosen for usefulness to readers. If NovelNest later displays advertising or sponsored material, payment does not determine the conclusions of ordinary editorial articles. Sponsored or paid material should be clearly identified as such.

Sources and accuracy

When an article discusses a specific novel, author, publication status, or measurable fact, NovelNest should rely on the site catalog, the authorized source, or another reliable source. General genre explainers may describe common conventions without claiming that every story in a genre follows the same pattern.

Corrections

If an editorial page contains a factual error, readers can report it through the Contact page. Confirmed errors should be corrected without hiding the substance of the change.

Clear separation from licensed fiction

Novel text and original NovelNest editorial writing serve different purposes. A licensed chapter is presented as the author's work. A Reading Desk article is NovelNest editorial content and should be labeled as an original guide.
